solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Empty box protecting organ

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps around it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to box someone is to clout them, a heavy blow
the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone describes an empty box shielding a body organ, as if packed for transplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container noun but is the verb to hit; 'Empty' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear out a cupboard or room is to empty it of its contents, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: It becomes girl in large town to be elegant

indicators.note: one thing becomes another, so the named word is swapped out for its replacement

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters leave
a lass is a girl
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Moving to the big city makes a girl sophisticated.
explanation.walkthrough: In CITY the letters IT are replaced by LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Classy is informal for stylish and sophisticated, a synonym of elegant.

clue.text: Tesla possibly included in Joy's promotion

indicators.note: being included in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: elation is joy
a Tesla is an example of an EV, an electric vehicle

explanation.surface: Joy has been promoted, perhaps rewarded with a Tesla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joy' looks like a woman's name; the possessive 's is the container's host.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation is a raising to higher rank, which is what a promotion is.

clue.text: Vital chemical ran out?

blocks.note: surface reading: an essential substance has been used up
setter's reading: the letters of 'ran' let out into a new order spell the familiar three-letter abbreviation for this chemical of life

explanation.surface: Supplies of some essential chemical have run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation RNA is an anagram of 'ran', hinted at by 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: This nucleic acid carries genetic messages in every living cell, so it is literally vital, essential to life.

clue.text: Finished drunk and on edge

blocks.note: time is up when it is finished
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone who has finished drinking is drunk and jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight means tense and anxious, the same state as being nervous or on edge.

clue.text: Cricket side close to revolt

blocks.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a close is an end or conclusion

explanation.surface: A cricket team is on the brink of mutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field the batter faces; 'revolt' is the verb meaning disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to disgust or affront them, which is to give offence; verb synonym.

clue.text: Hums rendition of Wasted Time

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked, so these letters are ruined and rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at a hummed version of a song called Wasted Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted Time' reads as a song title but splits into anagram indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics time is treated as the fourth dimension after length, breadth and height.

clue.text: The beginning of Evil Dead bringing cheer

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of Evil
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: The opening of the horror film Evil Dead somehow lifts the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Evil Dead is a horror film, a jarring source of cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with high spirits, so it is to cheer someone as a verb.

clue.text: Detectives essentially split up

blocks.note: DIs are detective inspectors
per se is Latin for in essence

explanation.surface: The detectives have basically gone their separate ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' looks like an adverb on the surface but supplies the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter or break up, as a crowd splits up and goes in different directions.

clue.text: Restaurant has tail of lobster in gravy

indicators.note: the tail is the back end, so only the last letter is kept
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Bisto is a well-known British brand of gravy granules
last letter of lobster

explanation.surface: A restaurant serves its lobster tail in gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant, originally French.

clue.text: Top-notch crust of rhubarb tart

indicators.note: a crust is the outside of something, so only the outermost letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: ace means excellent
first and last letters of rhubarb

explanation.surface: A cook boasts of a first-class rhubarb tart with a fine crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like the pastry dish but is the adjective meaning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare word for sour or sharp-tasting, a direct synonym of tart as an adjective.

clue.text: Courts Romeo in a Butlin's resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, these letters are sorted again into a new order

blocks.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover goes wooing at a Butlin's holiday camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Butlin's is a chain of British holiday camps; 'resort' reads as re-sort, and 'Courts' is the noun, not the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribunals are judicial bodies that hear cases, so they are courts in the legal sense.

clue.text: Occasionally strange things drunk at male event

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so only every other letter is kept
drunk suggests reeling about, so these letters stagger into a new order
at here places one piece in the middle of the other, wrapped by it

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Odd things get drunk now and then at an all-male party.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters split in two to wrap around the middle piece; 'at' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag night is the British name for a groom's party with his male friends before the wedding.

clue.text: Keynote article by the author

blocks.note: the definite article
the setter, or author, refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A keynote piece of writing is credited to the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The author' is the crossword convention for the setter, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The keynote of a speech or work is its central idea, its main subject or motif.

clue.text: Game point Tom?

blocks.note: a tip is a pointed end
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A quizzical question whether Tom is the one to score the point.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipcat is an old street game in which a short tapered stick is struck at one end to make it fly up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is a traditional children's game played with a stick and a small wooden piece.

clue.text: Tragic hero serves up ideology, being somewhat reflective

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the run of words is used
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of serves, all of up, and the start of ideology

explanation.surface: A thoughtful tragic protagonist dishes out a philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus is the doomed king of Sophocles' plays, the archetypal hero of Greek tragedy.

clue.text: Ban for writer

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A writer faces a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but supplies PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe something is to forbid it officially, so it is a verb synonym of ban.

clue.text: Southern holidaymaker is one who's likely to peel

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a tripper is a holidaymaker, especially a day visitor

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in the sunny south is bound to get sunburnt and peel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sunburnt skin peeling; the answer peels off clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper performs by taking off clothes, a playful sense of peeling layers away.

clue.text: Pep with expression of triumph when reversing hybrid

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the shout is read from end to start

blocks.note: pep and tang both mean zest or sharpness
the bullfight cheer

explanation.surface: Someone shouts with gusto after backing a winning hybrid car.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit bred as a cross between a tangerine and a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Invest in road building

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are assembled into a new structure

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor puts money into road building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' looks financial but means to install someone in office.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to confer office on them; to ordain is to install a priest, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Fool dropping the first bit of puzzle

indicators.note: dropping the first bit means losing the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to flummox is to baffle or puzzle

explanation.surface: An idiot drops the opening piece of a jigsaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' is the verb: FLUMMOX loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: A lummox is a clumsy, stupid person, an informal word for a fool or oaf.

clue.text: Plate of honey eaten by tellytubby

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Laa-Laa is one of the Teletubbies, children's TV characters, here written short
mel is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy

explanation.surface: A Teletubby scoffs a plate of honey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Teletubbies are characters from a British children's TV show; Laa-Laa is the yellow one, its spelling trimmed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamella is a thin plate or layer, as in the gills of a mushroom or in bone.

clue.text: Creeps in Red Square? Just the leader

indicators.note: only the leader means just the front letter of the word before is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
Che Guevara, the revolutionary, as a Red
first letter of Square

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks through Red Square in Moscow, but only partway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Square' reads as the Moscow landmark but splits: Red is the communist Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move very slowly, a step at a time, as one does when creeping.

clue.text: Bond is topless superhuman

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, standing in for a type of bond

indicators.note: with no top, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: bionic powers are superhuman, as in the Bionic Man

explanation.surface: James Bond is revealed as a shirtless superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is the chemistry term: an ionic bond holds ions together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ionic bond is a chemical link formed by attraction between oppositely charged ions.

clue.text: Irritable chest in city

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: NY is New York
an ark is a chest or coffer

explanation.surface: Someone has a grumpy feeling in their chest in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Narky is British slang for bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Narky is informal British for sarcastic and bad-tempered, a slang synonym of irritable.

clue.text: West Indian brother

blocks.note: first meaning: a person from Dominica or the ... Republic
second meaning: a friar of the order founded by St Dominic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' suggests a sibling but means a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Caribbean islander and a friar of the Order of Preachers, a religious brother.

clue.text: Narrow-minded friend transfixed by a mixed choir

indicators.note: something transfixed is pierced right through, so the other piece runs through its middle
mixed means stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bigoted chum is stopped in their tracks by a choir of mixed voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial, literally of a parish, has come to mean having a limited, small-town outlook.

clue.text: Sage, second one to take lead in race

definitions.note: the answer names a people as an adjective or collective noun

indicators.note: the later letter i jumps from the back to the front, taking the lead

blocks.note: a rishi is a Hindu sage or seer

explanation.surface: A herb gets a second wind and moves into the lead in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sage' looks like the herb but is the wise man; RISHI's final I (one) moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish are a people or nation, so race here means an ethnic group, not a contest.

clue.text: Year in Moroccan home close to Marrakech city

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is kept

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a riad is a traditional Moroccan house built round a courtyard
last letter of Marrakech

explanation.surface: A year spent in a Moroccan house near Marrakech.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Daddy Cool, not so free from stress

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
in means fashionable
less means to a lower degree

explanation.surface: Dad is not as relaxed as he looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something painless causes no pain or trouble, so it comes free of strain or difficulty.
